links.outcome: Share of questions with relevant, evidence-based answers, RAG systems versus general-purpose LLMs
links.effect: General-purpose LLMs gave relevant, evidence-based answers for 2-10% of questions; the RAG-based OpenEvidence gave them for 24%, and the agentic ChatRWD for 58%. OpenEvidence was actionable for 48% of questions with existing evidence, versus <5% for the general-purpose LLMs.
links.quote: General-purpose LLMs rarely produced relevant, evidence-based answers (2-10% of questions).

unlisted_practices: Using an agentic LLM that generates new real-world-data evidence when published literature is lacking

screen.reason: Evaluates physician actionability and accuracy of clinical question answering comparing baseline general-purpose LLMs against retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and an agentic real-world data pipeline.

primary.practice: retrieval-augmented generation and agentic data extraction
